content.title: Our actions to protect our environment and food chain | Danone Group
content.text: What is regenerative agriculture? Future-proofing our farms At Danone, we believe that regenerative agriculture is a holistic, outcome-based approach to farming, that benefits the planet, people, and animals. Regenerative Agriculture focuses on enhancing soil health, boosting biodiversity, and conserving water resources, while promoting animal welfare and supporting farmers livelihoods through increased farm resilience and profitability. Through innovation, regenerative practices and strong partnerships, Danone aims to maximize agriculture’s positive impacts, creating sustainable and resilient farming systems. Managing water resources Water is a precious resource that’s central to health and our business. Through our sustainability strategy, the Danone Impact Journey, we’ve set the target of improving water access for 30 million people by 2030. We’re also developing plans to preserve and restore watersheds in high water-stressed areas where we operate by 2030, and use our 4R approach (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Reclaim) in all our production sites. Why is packaging so important? Driving the transition to a circular packaging system Packaging is essential for Danone's products as it protects food and beverages, guaranteeing safe delivery to our consumers, extending shelf life and reducing food waste. It also serves as a key touchpoint for our brands, conveying important information and enhancing the consumer experience. However, traditional linear packaging systems often result in significant waste and environmental impact. That’s why Danone strives to offer nutritious, high-quality food and beverages in packaging that is circular. This means that Danone's ambition for all packaging is to design it to be safely reused or recycled in order to keep the materials used in the economy and never become waste or pollution. Limiting food loss and waste More than a billion tons of food is wasted each year. It’s both a waste of resources, with a social and financial costs, and a contributor to greenhouse gas emissions. That's why we’ve set the goal of reducing food waste by 50% by 2030, compared to 2020 levels, in line with the United Nation's Sustainable Development Goal 12.3. Sourcing sustainably All our suppliers are required to follow Danone’s Sustainability Principles for Business Partners or our Sustainable Sourcing Policy ensuring shared standards and commitment to sourcing material and services sustainably. Suppliers are also invited to go further and co-create solutions for shared growth. Our Partner for Growth program is a key element of our Renew Danone strategy and will shape the way we engage with our suppliers in the future. By collaborating with organizations from start-ups to academic institutions, we aim to boost innovation and explore new consumer trends - all while adopting responsible and sustainable business practices.
